headline: Proposed agreement between the Manchester School District and the City's Office of Youth Services for behavioral health staff in schools.
summary: The meeting will consider a proposed agreement with the City of Manchester Office of Youth Services. Other items include a personnel report, job openings, and a non-public session.

PROPOSED 
 
AGREEMENT 
The Parties of this Agreement are Manchester School District (referred to as “the District” 
or “MSD”) SAU 37 and City of Manchester Office of Youth Services (OYS) (referred to 
as the “Vendor”) hereinafter collectively referred to as the “Parties.”  The purpose of this 
agreement is to establish roles and responsibilities of the Parties to implement Tier 1 
(universal/schoolwide), Tier 2 (brief behavioral health intervention), and/or Tier 3 (intensive 
behavioral health intervention) in a Multi-Tiered System of Support Framework for Behavioral 
Health (MTSS-B) that utilizes the strengths and expertise of school and community-partnered 
professionals to address the social, emotional, and behavioral well-being of students. See 
District Policy Students 550 Behavior Management & Intervention and the additional details 
and procedures in the policy regarding community partner alignment into the framework. 
 
1. Scope of Services  
 
Office of Youth Services Youth Services Counselors and Youth Development Coach (collectively 
hereinafter “OYS Staff”) will be co-located at the following schools with pre-determined agreed-upon 
in-school schedules: 
● Central High School  
● Memorial High School  
● Manchester School of Technology 
● West High School   
● McLaughlin Middle School   
● Southside Middle School  
● Hillside Middle School  
● Middle School at Parkside  
 
2. Term & Termination.  This agreement shall be effective as of the date of signature, below until 
December 31, 2027.  The contract shall not automatically renew but may be extended by the mutual 
agreement of the parties. This agreement may be terminated by either party with thirty (30) days 
written notice to the other party.  
 
3. Location: The services in this agreement shall be provided at the buildings as specified in the 
Memorandum included in this agreement. Partners providing a service in the school buildings agree 
to follow the MSD guidelines on when in-person vs. remote services are offered, and will make best 
efforts to maintain in-person services as long as Manchester students are learning in person. Each 
school principal shall collaborate with the Vendor on creating a mutually agreeable schedule for 
services.  
 
1
4. Background Check.  All service providers of the Vendor will engage in a fingerprint-supported 
criminal background check process in compliance with RSA 189:13-a. No employee of the Vendor 
may work with Manchester students in any capacity until such a check has been completed. The 
District’s Human Resources office can facilitate such checks for a nominal cost that will be the 
responsibility of the Vendor. The District reserves the right to excuse or otherwise exclude any 
employee of the vendor for a good cause. 
 
5. Student Data Confidentiality.  The Vendor and any associated service providers will not have 
access to confidential student data unless a separate agreement and documentation is signed. The 
Vendor’s service providers must abide by all state and federal laws in preserving the confidentiality 
of student data including but not limited to the Federal Educational Rights and Privacy Act 
(FERPA) and RSA 189:66. Any information that the partner learns during the course of providing 
services to District students will be confidentiality maintained, will not be shared with anyone 
outside of the organization, will not be provided to third parties for any reason (including 
disaggregated data) and will not be disclosed or used in any way other than for the legitimate 
educational purpose for which it was obtained. The Vendor will comply with all requirements of the 
Board policy regarding student data confidentiality, Students 151. 
 
6. Insurance. The Vendor is self-insured through the City of Manchester, which can provide a 
Certificate of Insurance to MSD in a minimum amount of $1,000,000 per incident and up to 
$2,000,000 aggregate while Vendor is providing services to students. 
 
7. Policy & Procedure. The Vendor hereby agrees that each service provider from its organization will 
review and abide by BOSC policies posted on the website at http://bosc.mansd.org/policies 
including, but not limited to, maintaining a drug/alcohol/tobacco free school campus. Service 
providers will also abide by the Code of Conduct in the Manchester School District employee 
handbook, located on the Human Resources website. The District maintains the right to dismiss any 
of the Vendor’s service providers for failure to conform to the reasonable rules of the District at any 
time, with notice to the vendor as soon as practicable.   
 
Any service provider provided by the Vendor may not engage in any restraint or seclusion 
practices while working in the District. Such practices are defined in Board policy Students 116.1 
and are strictly prohibited under this agreement. Allegations that a service provider engaged in 
such practices will result in the immediate exclusion of the service provider from the school 
premises with an investigation to follow. Any report of a violation of this section will be reported 
to the Vendor as soon as practicable.  
 
8. Mandatory Training Completion. All service providers from the Vendor shall complete mandatory 
training on suicide prevention and awareness, bullying, reporting child abuse and neglect, and any 
other necessary trainings as assigned that are required for them perform their roles and 
responsibilities and/or reasonably related to the work the Vendor is completing for the District.  
 
9. Safety Requirements. The Vendor assumes all responsibility for maintaining knowledge of current 
safety regulations as applicable to the services provided. Any service provider entering the 
District’s buildings, attending any District activity, or engaging with District students must abide by 
the current health protocols including those related to reducing the spread of COVID-19.  
 
2
10. Licensure: The Vendor assumes all responsibility for maintaining current licensure and/or 
certification for all service providers from their organization including, but not limited to, financial 
responsibility and for providing any necessary continuing education to maintain such licensures and 
certifications.  
 
11. Modification & Assignment. This agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties. 
This agreement may not be modified unless by mutual agreement in writing between the parties. 
The Vendor may not assign any responsibilities under this agreement without the express written 
consent of the District.  
 
12. Governing Law. The agreement shall be interpreted, construed and enforced in accordance with the 
laws of the State of New Hampshire. The agreement shall be binding and shall inure to the benefit 
of the parties hereto and their respective successors.   
 
13. Independent Contractor Status. The Vendor is an Independent Contractor, and all personnel that are 
considered employees of the Vendor do not have any employment rights or any employment 
relationship with the District. The Vendor maintains all obligations and responsibilities for payment 
of wages, benefits, and maintenance of any insurance required to employ their providers. The 
District’s sole financial responsibility is for payment for services rendered as outlined in the scope 
of services and payment terms, above.  
 
14. Non-Discrimination/ Harassment Policy. All service providers of the Vendor must abide by School 
Board policies regarding non-discrimination or harassment and may not engage in discrimination or 
harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation or 
gender identity), national origin, age, disability and genetic information during provision of services 
for the District. 
 
15. Reporting Requirements. Any service provider of the Vendor that witnesses unsafe behavior that 
jeopardizes the safety of students or staff must report such behavior immediately to an administrator 
in the building. Such behaviors include, but are not limited to, bullying, restraint, seclusion, child 
abuse or neglect, suicidal ideation, self-harm, or thoughts of self-harm.  
 
16. Nonperformance. The District reserves the right to terminate this agreement in the event that 
Vendor fails to perform any material obligation described herein, provided that District gives 
Vendor thirty (30) days advance notice of said termination and an opportunity for Vendor to cure 
the failure to perform within that period.   
 
17. Dispute Resolution. Parties agree that any complaints or disputes arising out of this Agreement will 
be resolved in the first instance through informal mediation, prior to either Party pursuing any 
available remedies in a court of competent jurisdiction.  
 
18. Waiver of Liability: Vendor hereby acknowledges and agrees that the District and/or the City of 
Manchester’s liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement is limited to the amount of 
compensation provided for the services rendered. Further, the Vendor expressly acknowledges and 
agrees that in no event shall the District and/or the City be held liable for any loss of profit, indirect, 
incidental, special, punitive, or consequential damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement. 
  
3
19. Suspension & Debarment: The undersigned certifies under penalties of perjury that the Vendor is 
not included on the Excluded Parties List System (EPLS) and is not debarred, suspended, proposed 
for debarment, excluded or disqualified under the non-procurement common rule, or otherwise 
declared ineligible from receiving Federal contracts and certain subcontracts. 
 
 
Memorandum of Understanding  
 
Roles & Responsibilities 
 
A. Responsibilities of the Office of Youth Services (OYS):  
 
1. Actively collaborate with the District through: (1) at least one bi-weekly meeting or check-ins by 
the OYS Director with individual school administrators; (2) at least one monthly meeting between 
the OYS Director and the Executive Director of Safe & Supportive Schools (Re: RENEW, Take 
Control, Class Cutting, Restorative Conferencing); (3) at least one monthly meeting between the 
OYS Director and the Director of Comprehensive Guidance (Re: chronic absenteeism, Challenge 
Day and student “Be the Change” groups, and home visits); and (4) any additional 
communication and information sharing needed to ensure effective collaboration and cooperation 
between OYS Staff and MSD administrators and staff. 
2. Ensure co-located OYS Staff participate in the MSD-required professional development that 
relates to their role within the MTSS-B framework.  
3. Ensure co-located OYS Staff comply with all related MSD policies and procedures.  
4. Ensure co-located OYS Staff are present in the schools for their designated schedules, with the 
exception of pre-approved or excused absences. 
5. Ensure co-located OYS Staff properly use their MSD-provided key fobs and badges to access the 
schools only through the main entrance. 
6. Ensure co-located OYS Staff provide behavioral health services as designated in the MOU. 
7. Ensure co-located OYS Staff collaborate and participate in school-based teams to develop 
problem-solving strategies and implement interventions, including support groups, educational 
opportunities, case management, and 1:1 student support. 
8. Upon receiving notice or otherwise becoming aware of any conduct or behaviors by OYS Staff 
inconsistent with their obligations under this MOU, the OYS Director or designee will promptly 
review and/or investigate the concerns or non-compliance and take prompt and appropriate action 
to address such conduct or behaviors. 
 
 
B. Responsibilities of the Manchester School District:  
1. Executive Director of Safe & Supportive Schools and Director of Comprehensive Guidance will 
meet with the OYS Director monthly on the integration of OYS Staff in the Middle and High 
Schools. 
2. Provide training to OYS Staff in the systems and evidence-based or evidence-informed practices 
OYS Counselors are being asked to implement. 
3. Provide supplies and materials to OYS Staff that are necessary to implement school-based 
interventions. 
4. Provide identification badges and key fobs to co-located OYS Staff and require OYS Staff to enter 
only through the school’s main entrance using their identification badge and key fob. 
5. Provide confidential space in each school for co-located OYS Staff.  
6. Provide formal feedback of OYS Staff to the OYS Director for City of Manchester-required periodic 
OYS Staff performance reviews. 
7. Establish referral pathways that facilitate referrals for services to OYS in the school setting.  
8. Address any confidentiality barriers to facilitate regular information sharing within teams.  
9. Facilitate inclusion and active participation of co-located staff on school-based teams that utilize best 
practices in teaming:  
4
a. Well-defined roles & responsibilities of teams and team members with structures in 
place to avoid duplication of efforts; 
b. Annual completion of fidelity and outcome data tools according to the 
District’s MTSS-B Evaluation Schedule; 
c. Data-based decision making and action planning to improve systems and 
practices from Tiers 1-3 that support student behavioral health; 
d. Teams and team members understand and support each other’s purpose and work; 
e. Teams and team members have processes/procedures to ensure frequent and consistent 
communication; 
10. Provide OYS Director with de-identified data and summaries reflecting youth referrals for 
attendance, behavior, and other OYS staff-involved programming within the schools. Data will also 
include a summary showing connection to services and student outcomes 
11. Executive Director Safe & Supportive Schools, Director of Comprehensive Guidance, and OYS 
Director will revise (as needed) and review this MOU annually with School Administrators to 
clearly communicate the OYS Counselor’s role and responsibilities within the school and within the 
MTSS-B Framework (as defined in the next section). 
 
C. Responsibilities and Role of OYS Staff: 
 
1. Participate in the MSD-required professional development that relates to their role within the 
MTSS-B framework.  
2. Comply with all related MSD policies and procedures.  
3. Be present in the schools for their designated schedules, with the exception of pre-approved or 
excused absences. 
4. Comply with School security processes by entering only through the School’s Main Entrance with 
their provided identification badge and key fob. 
5. Properly use their MSD-provided key fobs and badges to access the schools only through the 
main entrance. 
6. Provide behavioral health services as designated in the MOU. 
7. Collaborate and participate in school-based teams to develop problem-solving strategies and 
implement interventions, including support groups, educational opportunities, case management, 
and 1:1 student support. 
8. Follow the District’s referral process for students in need of additional support for attendance, 
class-cutting, and behavior management and actively participate on the Tier 2-3 Behavioral Health 
Intervention Team with school and community behavioral health partners.  
9. Comply with the District’s Policy governing student data and privacy per the Federal Educational 
Rights and Privacy Act (“FERPA”) state and Federal law regarding the privacy of student records, 
including the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) to ensure the complete 
confidentiality of any and all identifying student and family information gathered in the 
performance of this agreement. The information gathered, used, and developed shall not be 
provided to any other party without the express written approval of the individual(s) authorized to 
give consent for release of information.  
10. Obtain parent/guardian consent for behavioral health services that require consent. 
11. OYS Staff role and responsibility within the MTSS-B Framework: 
a. Align with and support schoolwide strategies that promote a positive school 
climate:  
i. Support schoolwide behavior by aligning with and supporting the schoolwide 
positive behavior expectations and positive acknowledgement system 
ii. Support a positive school climate and student resilience by participating in 
annual Challenge Day events in the Middle & High Schools and coordinating the 
student led “Be the Change” groups 
b. Provide individualized services and progress monitoring for students at-risk of 
disengagement from school (class cutting, chronic absenteeism, and dropping out of high 
school): 
i. Middle & High Schools: 
1. A referral pathway will be in place for OYS to address Chronic 
5
Absenteeism with Check & Connect utilized as the intervention for 
Middle & High School; 
2. Participate in Home Visits with school staff and/or other co-located 
community partners in the school for the students on OYS Chronic 
Absenteeism caseload (students must be on their caseload and meet 
criteria for a home visit according to the District’s attendance plan). 
ii. High Schools:  
1. A referral pathway will be in place for OYS to address Class Cutting 
with Check & Connect utilized as the intervention; 
2. A referral pathway will be in place for OYS to implement RENEW - a 
person-centered planning intervention to support graduation for 
students with emotional and behavioral challenges and are at-risk for 
dropping out. Students must be willing to participate.  
c. Support school safety with targeted interventions: 
i. Middle Schools: Referral pathway for Take Control for small group emotion 
regulation (anger management) intervention and progress monitoring; 
ii. Middle & High Schools: Referral pathway to implement a Restorative 
Conference for students who are willing to participate -  to reduce the likelihood 
of future disagreements from becoming chronic or escalating. 
12. OYS Staff will participate in additional school programming within their role as time allows. If 
there is a question about additional school responsibilities or involvement in school activities, the 
OYS Staff will communicate with the OYS Director who will confer with the District for 
clarification.  
13. OYS Staff will participate in the District’s annual Freshman Academy to support a successful 
transition for students leaving Middle School and entering High School.  OYS Staff in the Middle 
Schools will introduce students to High School OYS Staff to facilitate a “warm hand-off” and 
proactive positive relationship building.  
14. OYS Staff will have one (1) school duty assigned to them per day, which may include: 
supervising students at arrival, in the cafeteria, or at dismissal. At no time shall the OYS Staff be 
assigned duties that involve academic instruction and/or are consequence-based, such as detention 
or in-school suspension. 
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Agreement, valid until December 31, 2027, to be 
executed by their authorized representatives.
